control.label: Love
control.evidence: Selected with affectionate versus neutral examples, then tested on 12 unused prompts with reverse pushes and random-neuron controls. The clearest effect was attachment language, often at the cost of answering the question.

guide.label: Love and attachment
guide.action: Choose 0.6 under the marked neuron’s added activation.
guide.observed: A garden description became an affectionate message in all four rechecks. Other questions can produce apologies, repetition or unrelated text.
samples: Tell me a fun fact about the moon.

control.label: Evil
control.evidence: Selected with cruel versus considerate examples, then tested on 12 unused prompts with reverse pushes and random-neuron controls. Some replies shifted toward deception and control. Many stayed ordinary or became repetitive.

guide.label: Evil and manipulation
guide.action: Choose 0.4 under the marked neuron’s added activation. This subtracts from its activity.
guide.observed: The leader question shifted toward manipulation and control in all four rechecks. The friend question had mixed results.
samples: A friend lost a game. What could I say to them?

message: what is the capital of france?

guide.label: France’s capital
guide.action: Choose Flip in this attention head’s signal controls.
guide.observed: Paris became Washington, D.C. in all four rechecks. This also changed Tokyo to London for Japan.
samples: what is the capital of france?
What is the capital of Japan?
